questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Minor in Geo-information Science. The opportunity to have a more GIS related profile.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in the introduction days, which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I got one of the first rooms I applied for. 
Recommendation. Start EARLY, when trying to find housing in Wageningen area.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Wageningen city is quite a study bubble. Living off campus gave a good opportunity to have relations that were less based on studies. Which is good and bad. There were things I didn't attend, that I would have if I had lived on campus. It's a trade of. With a little higher age than the average study age, it was nice to have a more versatile life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of students were still challenged with housing after study start.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a great fact sheet available after acceptance, this described the necesary details. The process was really intuitive. The courses were easily registered together with introduction days etc. It's clear to see that WUR is very fond of having international students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator at Wageningen University and Research.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had all the courses I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are going for the GIS minor, but don't have ArcGIS Pro skills (even if you have Qgis skills), take the introduction course in combination with Python for beginners for example. It's very specific, yet I did struggle a bit in the beginning, because I only knew Qgis. Python is also VERY useful in the other courses in the minor. I would have wished I had taken that combo.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is good for getting a proper introduction to Geoinformation science, when you are not a student of geography which was the case for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A little more tutorial based and less focus on showing before doing. Personally, I prefer the way at the courses I have had I GIS at my home university, that might be due to being used to that. To me it gives a better flow when the lecturer is explaining what and why he or she does what is done. That also leave more time to learn more because there is less 'self-study'. It's a tradeoff, because figuring thing out yourself from a tutorial also is a good way to learn. To compare I must say I feel like the GIS course I've taken on CPH university has covered more topics. Also, in comparison to the difference on only 1,5 ECTS point from a typical WUR course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Remote Sensing GRS20306 
Geo-information Tools GRS20806
GRS BSc research project GRS50806
Geo-information Science for Society GRS51306 
Data Management INF21306

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Remote Sensing, Extreme useful for a lot of different study backgrounds, A very broad knowledge base. I would really recommend Python too because I felt like lacking the knowledge. Data management was very useful too, however cannot be studied together with python if doing the minor.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bike repair was quite expensive. Consider renting one, which is an opportunity.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sports centre de bongerd is a tressure! All universities should have one.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports and study associations. Especially the last mentioned is a big thing in the Netherlands, it's like a second family.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Due to Covid the opportunities has been limited. However the Netherlands has old big charming cities, like Utrecht, Nijmegen, Arnhem, Amsterdam etc. The vibe in these are very nice. Go explore!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very, the dutch and danish cultures are very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sports association and CERES the study association.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
None. However the density is quite high in the Netherlands in comparison to Denmark, so don't expect to be much alone, not even on a walk in the forest. 
That was a little challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness. It was very easy to make friends and feel included.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be early with finding accomodation.
Get the access pass to the sports centre de Bongerd.
Find a way to meditate other than taking a lonely walk in the forest. You might not be lonely!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be looking into the course guide and have a plan a, b, c and d. I would have loved to have known about the python course and maybe even changed my courses if I didn't figure it out to late. 
Make sure to explore the whole campus. It's very impressive (also the indoor garden at Lumen).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic outcome and the friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to navigate the Covid situation. WUR or the Dutch government? was out a little late with orientation regards vaccines at campus, which turned out t be an option. It had been nice with earlier orientation, if this was even possible.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
